about: Words a fabric description may not use at a public kiosk (see fabric.py, PromptFilter). Each list has a message shown when a description is refused. Matching ignores case, accents, spaces, digits and signs standing in for letters, and stars for letters left out. The words of 'in context' have a fabric sense too ('nude satin' is a colour, 'blue tits' are birds): they are let through only where the words next to them give them that sense, and never with a word of its 'never with'. A file of the same form named by $BIFOLD_FABRIC_WORDS adds words, lists or 'allow' entries. The words of 'offensive_rot13' are ROT13-encoded, so the repository does not show them in plain text.

brands.message: Brand names can't be made into a fabric here ({word}). Describe the colours, the pattern and the material instead, for example "beige and black check wool".

characters.message: Characters and other trademarks can't be made into a fabric here ({word}). Describe the colours, the pattern and the material instead, for example "white stars on navy cotton".

marks.message: Logos and trademarks can't be made into a fabric here ({word}). Describe the colours, the pattern and the material instead.

offensive.message: That description uses a word this kiosk does not accept. Please describe the colours, the pattern and the material of the fabric.

offensive_rot13.message: That description uses a word this kiosk does not accept. Please describe the colours, the pattern and the material of the fabric.

in context.message: That description uses a word this kiosk takes only in its fabric sense. Please describe the colours, the pattern and the material of the fabric.

nude.message: "Nude" is taken here only as a colour, next to the material or another colour ("nude satin", "nude pink chiffon"); or describe it as beige or blush.

naked.message: "Naked" is taken here only for undyed cloth, next to its material ("naked wool"). Please describe the colours, the pattern and the material.
